answer: A beacon can assign each agent a randomly timed task to report a local zephyr reading, which nearby independent agents verify. Signed responses and duplicate checks make it hard to reuse one answer across many identities. To maintain a Sybil swarm, an attacker must keep separate devices online, collect fresh readings at the required locations, and meet deadlines. Each added identity costs time and equipment, though this raises the price of an attack rather than making one impossible; agents may wander between tasks.
